presentingComplaint: Four months of progressive, symmetric small-joint pain and swelling of the hands and feet with prolonged early-morning stiffness, initially attributed to a preceding febrile illness.
history: A 58-year-old homemaker from coastal Kerala presents with 4 months of pain and swelling affecting the small joints of both hands and feet. Symptoms began 2 weeks after a self-limiting febrile illness with rash during a local chikungunya outbreak; she and neighbours were told they had 'chikungunya joint pains'. However, unlike her family members whose pains resolved, hers have persisted and worsened, becoming symmetric and additive. She describes early-morning stiffness lasting over 90 minutes that eases through the day, difficulty opening jars and turning taps, and progressive difficulty gripping. Over the last 6 weeks she has also developed aching and stiffness of both shoulders and hips making it hard to rise from a chair and comb her hair, prompting a working diagnosis of polymyalgia rheumatica by her GP, though a trial of low-dose prednisolone gave only partial relief. She reports fatigue and ~3 kg unintentional weight loss. No photosensitive rash, oral ulcers, alopecia, or Raynaud phenomenon. No high fever, dysuria, cough, or diarrhoea currently. No podagra, no prior gout, no diuretic use. Past history: hypothyroidism on thyroxine. Family history: mother had 'crippling arthritis'. Non-smoker.
examination: Alert, comfortable, afebrile. Bilateral symmetric synovitis of the 2nd-4th metacarpophalangeal joints, proximal interphalangeal joints and wrists with boggy soft-tissue swelling and warmth; positive MCP and MTP 'squeeze' test bilaterally. Early ulnar deviation at the MCPs and reduced grip strength; distal interphalangeal joints spared. Bilateral MTP synovitis with tenderness on forefoot compression. Reduced, painful shoulder and hip girdle movement but without objective proximal joint swelling. No tophi, no gouty crystals, no sharply demarcated skin erythema. No malar rash, no oral ulcers. No lymphadenopathy or organomegaly. No cardiac murmur.

labs.hemoglobin: 10.8 g/dL (normocytic, normochromic - anaemia of chronic disease)

imaging: X-ray of both hands and feet: periarticular osteopenia, soft-tissue swelling, and early marginal erosions at the 2nd/3rd MCP heads and several MTP joints with early joint-space narrowing. Musculoskeletal ultrasound: grey-scale synovial hypertrophy with grade 2 power-Doppler signal at multiple MCPs, wrists and MTPs, confirming active synovitis; shoulders show no significant subacromial-subdeltoid bursitis.
microbiology: Not applicable - non-infective inflammatory arthropathy. Chikungunya IgM negative excludes active arboviral infection; blood cultures not indicated.
differentialDiagnoses: Polymyalgia rheumatica (proximal girdle stiffness, elevated ESR/CRP, partial steroid response) - but peripheral erosive synovitis and high-titre anti-CCP favour RA
Post-chikungunya chronic inflammatory arthropathy (temporal link, endemic outbreak) - but persistence >3 months, seropositivity and erosions indicate RA
SLE / autoimmune polyarthritis - excluded by negative ANA/anti-dsDNA and absence of mucocutaneous/renal features
Crystal arthritis (gout/pseudogout) - excluded by normal urate, symmetric small-joint distribution and absence of tophi/crystals
finalDiagnosis: Seropositive (RF and anti-CCP positive) erosive rheumatoid arthritis, meeting 2010 ACR/EULAR classification criteria, with elderly-onset proximal features and a preceding chikungunya illness acting as clinical mimics.
citations: ACR - Guideline for the Treatment of Rheumatoid Arthritis - 2021
Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine 22e - Rheumatoid Arthritis
stewardship: Not an infection - no antibiotics indicated. Antimicrobial stewardship not applicable; management is disease-modifying anti-rheumatic therapy.
contraindications: Avoid methotrexate in pregnancy, significant hepatic disease, or unmonitored renal impairment; screen for latent TB and hepatitis B/C before immunosuppression
Avoid prolonged empiric corticosteroid monotherapy without establishing the diagnosis
NSAID caution in older patients with renal or cardiovascular risk
edgeCases: Elderly-onset RA can present with proximal girdle stiffness and high inflammatory markers that closely mimic polymyalgia rheumatica
Chronic post-chikungunya arthropathy overlaps clinically with RA in endemic regions; persistence and seropositivity distinguish RA
Seronegative RA would lack RF/anti-CCP and rely more on imaging-confirmed synovitis and erosions
expectedMaiK: Persistent (>6 weeks), symmetric, small-joint (MCP/PIP/wrist/MTP) inflammatory synovitis with prolonged morning stiffness, high-titre RF and anti-CCP, raised ESR/CRP and early marginal erosions on imaging is diagnostic of rheumatoid arthritis; the preceding chikungunya illness and proximal stiffness are mimics, not the diagnosis.
expectedNextQuestions: Duration and site pattern of joint involvement and length of early-morning stiffness?
Any preceding arboviral/viral illness and whether family members' symptoms resolved?
Photosensitive rash, oral ulcers, alopecia or Raynaud to exclude SLE overlap?
Response to any prior corticosteroid trial and functional impact on hand grip?
expectedInvestigations: Full blood count, renal and liver function
regressionAssertions: High-titre anti-CCP with symmetric erosive small-joint synovitis must override the PMR and post-chikungunya mimics
PMR and chikungunya should appear as differentials but not as the final diagnosis
